hypothesis: .station-verdict.go (L299) assigns color:var(--green) to the 'GO' verdict label in the Go/No-Go pre-SHIP gate panel (#gonogo). The panel subtitle reads 'All stations must be GO before SHIP is authorized' — it is a pre-admission readiness check, not an admission event. In the demo state, HER=GO and HAL=GO while LEDGER=HOLD, MAYOR=PENDING, FLIGHT=NO_GO, and the COMMIT button is disabled. A station voting GO means 'this station has observed and cleared its pre-condition' — not 'the object is admitted.' Using --green (SA-ADMITTED) for a pre-admission clearance verdict violates the one-meaning-per-color rule. SA palette maps 🔵 observed to --blue (#5b8af0, defined at L32 with dim/bg variants). Reassigning station-verdict.go to --blue — 'the station has observed and cleared' — is semantically accurate and requires no new palette token.

The sibling triplet (go/hold/pend) maps cleanly to (observed/breach/review) = (--blue/--red/--amber). No color is added; the semantic mapping is exact.
